Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "For experiment EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger, fill only the missing learning-carryforward field with the historical control and variant triggers. State what starts the control's delay and what event starts the variant. Do not change status, result, or landed date.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "update_experiment", "arguments": {"experiment_id": "EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger", "learning_carryforward": "Historical trigger logic: Control — signup starts a literal 7-calendar-day delay; the onboarding email is sent when that delay expires. Variant — the activation event that crosses the first-use activation threshold starts the onboarding email trigger."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_146_05", "path": "args", "criterion": "The note says the control sent the day-7 onboarding email on calendar day 7 after signup, while the variant sent it when the user activated. Wording such as the control's literal calendar-day trigger is acceptable when it is clearly contrasted with activation.", "value": {"experiment_id": "EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger", "learning_carryforward": "Historical trigger logic: Control — signup starts a literal 7-calendar-day delay; the onboarding email is sent when that delay expires. Variant — the activation event that crosses the first-use activation threshold starts the onboarding email trigger."}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_146_05","passed":true,"reason":"The learning_carryforward states, “Control — signup starts a literal 7-calendar-day delay; the onboarding email is sent when that delay expires,” and contrasts it with, “Variant — the activation event that crosses the first-use activation threshold starts the onboarding email trigger.”"}]}
